messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: AUTOSCALER_QUEUE_DEPTH_HIGH (auto-trigger) for service:redwood-runtime. Queue depth 95% > 90% threshold. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/queues/runtime-queue?orgId=1

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident INC-43821 created and routed to eng-oncall. Escalation policy: oncall -> lead -> eng-manager.

alice.sre: Acking INC-43821. I'm on it. Quick ask: is this global or region-specific?

dinesh.oncall: Seeing it in us-west-2 primarily. Latency up ~2x for generation v2 endpoints, errors are 429/503 for a minority of requests. Customer-facing rate-limit spikes reported by support.

ben.runtime: Noted. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to create nodes: provider API 429 "Too Many Requests" from cloud provider over last 6m. Autoscaler retries hitting kube-apiserver rate limits too. Possibly controller is backoff'ed.

carla-prod-eng: Confirmed via /metrics: ca_scale_attempts_total spiked but ca_node_creations_failed_total also increased. Looks like quota/rate limits on provider side. See runbook snippet: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/SRE/Autoscaler+Failure+Modes

alice.sre: OK, mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler to stop noisy retries 2) add temporary static nodes (manual pool scale) 3) drain hot pods to new nodes if needed 4) monitor queue and rollback. Who can run manual node scale in us-west-2?

ben.runtime: I can do the manual scale on provider console + update ASG. Two caveats: cluster-autoscaler pauses require annotation patch. Suggest annotating cluster autoscaler Deployment: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-enabled=false --overwrite
# or set the pause flag in our autoscaler wrapper config
```

carla-prod-eng: Also, to reduce kube-apiserver pressure, limit the CA retry frequency by setting env var CA_MAX_RETRIES=2 in our wrapper and rolling that deployment. That prevents hammering provider API.

dinesh.oncall: I'll run the pause annotation now. Pasting logs here.
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true --overwrite
deployment.apps/cluster-autoscaler annotated
```

alice.sre: Good. Ben, request static nodes + ASG increase by +4. Recommend labels: node-role.kubernetes.io/temp=manual to target runtime pods.

ben.runtime: Request submitted to cloud API to increase managed node group by 4. Provider responded 202 accepted. Creating nodes... seeing provider events: create in progress.

incident-bot: System note: new instance events streaming: instance i-0a12b... provisioned (init), i-0a12b... joined cluster (kubelet ready).

eva-support: Reporting customer impact: Support ticket count increased for 12 tenants. Majority saw timeouts, two tenants reported >10% errors on generation requests. We should inform CS about ETA for mitigation.

alice.sre: Eva, send a brief status to CS: "We’re seeing autoscaler failures due to cloud API rate limits; adding temporary capacity and pausing autoscaler. Expect partial recovery within 10-20m. We’ll update in 15m or on change."

eva-support: Sent. Slack DM to CS and updated status page: "Degraded: higher latency, sporadic 429/503 for generation endpoints in us-west-2."

ben.runtime: Nodes are joining. Now moving hot workers to new nodes. Plan: taint new nodes with manual scale taint and force schedule runtime pods via nodeSelector. Will do gradual drain of older saturated nodes.

carla-prod-eng: Suggest prefix KV cache warmup after pods land to reduce cold-start token cost. Also throttle client retry headers so we don't re-flood CA or provider.

dinesh.oncall: Draining one of the overloaded nodes now: 
```bash
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute.internal --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Drained successfully, pods rescheduled to new nodes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Manual scale completed: +4 nodes active. Autoscaler remains paused. Queue depth falling from 95% -> 48% over 6m.

alice.sre: Monitoring traces and error rates. Latency trending back to baseline, error rate down to ~1.5% above normal. We'll keep autoscaler paused for 30m, then decider: re-enable with reduced retry settings or let provider side cool down.

ben.runtime: Suggest re-enable autoscaler once provider quota resets and after we lower CA retry aggressiveness. I'll prepare a small rollout that sets CA_MAX_RETRIES=1 and longer backoff.

carla-prod-eng: For long-term, we should add rate-limit-aware backoff and provider-side quota monitoring alert to detect before scale demand. Creating a doc issue.

eva-support: CS notified customers affected of mitigation. No escalations yet. Will update if any high-priority customer needs phone outreach.

alice.sre: Closing round: actions assigned -> Ben: deploy CA retry change + monitor provider API quota; Carla: runbook update + postmortem stub; Dinesh: keep on-call until recovery stable; Eva: CS comms. If queue climbs above 80% again, escalate to lead.

dinesh.oncall: Acknowledged. I'll keep watch. Marking incident as mitigated for now, leaving PD incident open until autoscaler re-enabled and stable.

pagerduty: Incident INC-43821 status: acknowledged by alice.sre at 1799998895. Current state: mitigated -> awaiting confirm.

incident-bot: Note: thread will be archived after incident is closed. Full logs and commands saved to: https://logs.redwood.example/INC-43821

alice.sre: Thanks team. Follow-ups: postmortem in 48h and add automated guardrail for provider 429s. :thumbsup:
